name: Elishah
overview: Elishah is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Javan, mentioned in Genesis 10:4. Beyond this paternal link, Scripture does not provide further tribal or familial details. His brief mention situates him within the genealogy of the nations descending from Noah's sons.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishah means 'G-d saves,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew elements. This proper name, recorded in Genesis 10:4, highlights God's saving nature but was not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Elishah as the son of Javan, establishing his place within the genealogy of Javan's descendants. No additional family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Elishah's importance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical record of Genesis 10:4, which traces the descendants of Noah through Japheth. As a son of Javan, Elishah represents one of the early progenitors of peoples known in the biblical narrative, underscoring God's providential unfolding of nations. His mention contributes to the biblical understanding of the spread of humanity after the flood.
